# bluetooth-controller (device class)

> USB Bluetooth controllers — parked for power and radio silence, or switched off through BlueZ

The Bluetooth radio of a laptop or dongle, as the kernel sees it: a USB device (on the field laptop, the Bluetooth half of an Intel AX210 combo card, whose Wi-Fi half is on PCIe and is not this device) driven by btusb and managed by BlueZ.

## Devices in this class

- [intel-ax210-bluetooth](intel-ax210-bluetooth.md)

## Shared setup

Nothing to install; BlueZ is part of the desktop. The radio switch is `bluetoothctl power off` or the tray's toggle; park and wake are `hammunition hardware park bluetooth-controller` and `hammunition hardware wake bluetooth-controller`.

## Power control

This device can be parked and woken. Method: `usb_deauthorize`.

A parked USB Bluetooth controller is unconfigured, not unpowered at the port: btusb drops hci0, BlueZ sees the adapter vanish and every paired device (a headset, a keyboard) disconnects, and the port is only allowed to suspend. This does not cut the controller's supply. The lighter switch is BlueZ's own, `bluetoothctl power off`, which the helper's `radio off bluetooth` verb and the tray's Radios toggle are to wrap (planned, not yet released). It needs no root and keeps the adapter attached. Park a Bluetooth controller only when nothing you are using is Bluetooth: a Bluetooth mouse or keyboard goes with it. Parking has not been run on a controller here (unmeasured).

See [device power control](power-control.md) for what parking does to a machine, how to inspect it and how to reverse it.
